:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Given that $$
\displaystyle D=\dfrac{\textrm d^{2}}{\textrm d x^{2}}+3 \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}+5,
$$ what is $D(y)$ for $y=e^{- x}?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y) = a_{2}\dfrac{\textrm d^{2}y}{\textrm d x^{2}} + a_{1}\dfrac{\textrm dy}{\textrm d x} + a_0y
$$

with constant coefficients  $a_2 = 1, a_1 = 3,$ and $a_0 = 5.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({e}^{-x}) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}+5\right){e}^{-x} \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({e}^{-x})+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-x})+5{e}^{-x} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-{e}^{-x})+3\cdot (-{e}^{-x})+5{e}^{-x} \\  & ={e}^{-x}-3{e}^{-x}+5{e}^{-x} \\  & =3{e}^{-x}\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $$
\displaystyle D = \frac{d^{3}}{dx^{3}} - 2\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}} + 2\frac{d}{dx},
$$ what is $D(y)$ for $y = e^{x} + x$?

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{2}=1,{a}_{1}=2,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({e}^{-2x}+x) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right)({e}^{-2x}+x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({e}^{-2x}+x)+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-2x}+x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{e}^{-2x}+1)+2(-2{e}^{-2x}+1) \\  & =4{e}^{-2x}-4{e}^{-2x}+2 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{3}=2,{a}_{2}=0,{a}_{1}=-3,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({e}^{-x}+2) \\  & =\left(2\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right)({e}^{-x}+2) \\  & =2\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({e}^{-x}+2)-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-x}+2) \\  & =2\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(-{e}^{-x})-3\cdot (-{e}^{-x}) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-x})+3{e}^{-x} \\  & =-2{e}^{-x}+3{e}^{-x} \\  & ={e}^{-x}\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{3}=1,{a}_{2}=0,{a}_{1}=2,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right){\sin }^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({\sin }^{2}⁡x)+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sin }^{2}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)+2\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡2x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{2}=1,{a}_{1}=3,$ and ${a}_{0}=-2.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({e}^{2x}) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}-2\right){e}^{2x} \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({e}^{2x})+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{2x})-2\cdot {e}^{2x} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{e}^{2x})+3\cdot (2{e}^{2x})-2{e}^{2x} \\  & =4{e}^{2x}+6{e}^{2x}-2{e}^{2x} \\  & =8{e}^{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{2}=1,{a}_{1}=2,$ and ${a}_{0}=-5.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}-5\right)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))-5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))+2\cdot (3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))-5\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\  & =-9\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-5\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\  & =-14\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{2}=1,{a}_{1}=5,$ and ${a}_{0}=1.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}+1\right)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))+5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))+1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))+5\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+5\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) \\  & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{2}=1,{a}_{1}=-3,$ and ${a}_{0}=4.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({x}^{3}) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}+4\right){x}^{3} \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({x}^{3})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})+4\cdot {x}^{3} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2})-3\cdot (3{x}^{2})+4{x}^{3} \\  & =6x-9{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3} \\  & =4{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+6x\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients ${a}_{3}=1,{a}_{2}=4,{a}_{1}=4,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({e}^{-2x}) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+4\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right){e}^{-2x} \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({e}^{-2x})+4\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({e}^{-2x})+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-2x}) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(-2{e}^{-2x})+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{e}^{-2x})+4\cdot (-2{e}^{-2x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{e}^{-2x})+4\cdot 4{e}^{-2x}-8{e}^{-2x} \\  & =-8{e}^{-2x}+16{e}^{-2x}-8{e}^{-2x} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{2}=1,{a}_{1}=-2,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right)(\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-2(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{3}=1,{a}_{2}=-3,{a}_{1}=4,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}-3\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-3\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+4(\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-3(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{2}=1,{a}_{1}=1,$ and ${a}_{0}=2.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(2{x}^{3}-x+1) \\  & =\left(\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}+2\right)(2{x}^{3}-x+1) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(2{x}^{3}-x+1)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}-x+1)+2\cdot (2{x}^{3}-x+1) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6{x}^{2}-1)+(6{x}^{2}-1)+2(2{x}^{3}-x+1) \\  & =12x+6{x}^{2}-1+4{x}^{3}-2x+2 \\  & =4{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+10x+1\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Given that $$
\displaystyle D=x^2\dfrac{\textrm d^{3}}{\textrm d x^{3}}-5x \dfrac{\textrm d^{2}}{\textrm d x^{2}} +9\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x},
$$ what is $D(y)$ for $y=\ln{x}?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y) = f_{3}(x)\dfrac{\textrm d^{3}y}{\textrm d x^{3}} + f_{2}(x)\dfrac{\textrm d^{2}y}{\textrm d x^{2}} + f_{1}(x)\dfrac{\textrm dy}{\textrm d x} + f_0(x)y.
$$

with $f_3 = x^2, f_2 = -5x, f_1 = 9,$ and $f_0 = 0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =\left({x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}-5x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+9\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right)\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-5x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+9\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)-5x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)+9\cdot \left(\frac{1}{x}\right) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)-5x\left(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)+\frac{9}{x} \\  & ={x}^{2}\left(\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}\right)+\frac{5}{x}+\frac{9}{x} \\  & =\frac{2}{x}+\frac{5}{x}+\frac{9}{x} \\  & =\frac{16}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Given that $$
\displaystyle D = x^{2}\frac{d^{3}}{dx^{3}} - x\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}} + \frac{d}{dx},
$$ what is $D(y)$ for $y = x^{3}$?

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=x,{f}_{1}=2,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =\left(x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right)\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)+\frac{2}{x} \\  & =x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)+\frac{2}{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{x}+\frac{2}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=x,{f}_{1}=1,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({x}^{2}-2x) \\  & =\left(x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right)({x}^{2}-2x) \\  & =x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({x}^{2}-2x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-2x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x-2)+(2x-2) \\  & =2x+2x-2 \\  & =4x-2\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=2x,{f}_{1}=3,$ and ${f}_{0}=-2.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =\left(2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}-2\right)\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-2\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)+\frac{3}{x}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =2x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)+\frac{3}{x}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =-\frac{2}{x}+\frac{3}{x}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =\frac{1}{x}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}={x}^{2},{f}_{1}=3,$ and ${f}_{0}=2.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({x}^{2}-1) \\  & =\left({x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}+2\right)({x}^{2}-1) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({x}^{2}-1)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-1)+2({x}^{2}-1) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x)+3(2x)+2({x}^{2}-1) \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot 2+6x+2{x}^{2}-2 \\  & =4{x}^{2}+6x-2\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=x,{f}_{1}=2x,$ and ${f}_{0}=-3.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) \\  & =\left(x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}-3\right)\frac{1}{x} \\  & =x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)+2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)-3\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)+2x\left(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)-\frac{3}{x} \\  & =x\cdot \frac{2}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{2}{x}-\frac{3}{x} \\  & =\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{5}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=2x,{f}_{1}=3,$ and ${f}_{0}=4.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right) \\  & =\left(2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}+4\right)\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \\  & =2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right)+4\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \\  & =2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(-\frac{1}{2{x}^{3/2}}\right)+3\left(-\frac{1}{2{x}^{3/2}}\right)+\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}} \\  & =2x\cdot \frac{3}{4{x}^{5/2}}-\frac{3}{2{x}^{3/2}}+\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}} \\  & =\frac{3}{2{x}^{3/2}}-\frac{3}{2{x}^{3/2}}+\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}={x}^{2},{f}_{1}=-x,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(2{x}^{3}+4) \\  & =\left({x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right)(2{x}^{3}+4) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(2{x}^{3}+4)-x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}+4) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6{x}^{2})-x\cdot 6{x}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot 12x-6{x}^{3} \\  & =12{x}^{3}-6{x}^{3} \\  & =6{x}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=x,{f}_{1}=-1,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) \\  & =\left(x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right)\frac{1}{x} \\  & =x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)-\left(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right) \\  & =x\cdot \left(\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}\right)+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}={x}^{2},{f}_{1}=x,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+x) \\  & =\left({x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right)(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+x) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+x)+x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+x) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{2}{x}+1\right)+x\left(\frac{2}{x}+1\right) \\  & ={x}^{2}\left(-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\right)+x\left(\frac{2}{x}+1\right) \\  & =-2+2+x \\  & =x\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{3}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y.
$$

with ${f}_{3}={x}^{2},{f}_{2}=-2x,{f}_{1}=x,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D({x}^{4}) \\  & =\left({x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}-2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right){x}^{4} \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({x}^{4})-2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({x}^{4})+x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{4}) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(4{x}^{3})-2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{3})+x(4{x}^{3}) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(12{x}^{2})-2x(12{x}^{2})+4{x}^{4} \\  & ={x}^{2}(24x)-24{x}^{3}+4{x}^{4} \\  & =24{x}^{3}-24{x}^{3}+4{x}^{4} \\  & =4{x}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{3}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y.
$$

with ${f}_{3}={x}^{2},{f}_{2}=3x,{f}_{1}=-1,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) \\  & =\left({x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+3x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\right)\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)+3x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\left(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)+3x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)-\left(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}\right)+3x\left(\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}\right)+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{6}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{6}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=3{x}^{2},{f}_{1}=-x,$ and ${f}_{0}=-2.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(x-5) \\  & =\left(3{x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}-2\right)(x-5) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(x-5)-x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x-5)-2(x-5) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\cdot 0-x\cdot 1-2x+10 \\  & =10-3x\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
If $$
\displaystyle D(y)=y\dfrac{\textrm d^{3}y}{\textrm d x^{3}} - \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x} + y^3,
$$ then calculate $D(e^{3x}).$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y) = f_{3}(x,y)\dfrac{\textrm d^{3}y}{\textrm d x^{3}} +  f_{2}(x,y)\dfrac{\textrm d^{2}y}{\textrm d x^{2}} + f_{1}(x,y)\dfrac{\textrm dy}{\textrm d x} + f_0(x,y)y
$$

with $f_3 = y,  f_2 = 0,  f_1 = -1,$ and $f_0 = y^2.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y = e^{3x}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}D({e}^{x}) & ={e}^{3x}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({e}^{3x})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{3x})+{({e}^{3x})}^{3} \\  & ={e}^{3x}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(3{e}^{3x})-3\cdot {e}^{3x}+{e}^{9x} \\  & ={e}^{3x}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(9{e}^{3x})-3\cdot {e}^{3x}+{e}^{9x} \\  & =27{e}^{6x}-3\cdot {e}^{3x}+{e}^{9x} \\  & ={e}^{3x}({e}^{6x}+27{e}^{3x}-3)\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=y,{f}_{1}=-xy,$ and ${f}_{0}=2y.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y={e}^{2x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D({e}^{2x}) & ={e}^{2x}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({e}^{2x})-x({e}^{2x})\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{2x})+2({e}^{2x})^{2} \\  & ={e}^{2x}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{e}^{2x})-x{e}^{2x}\cdot 2{e}^{2x}+2{e}^{4x} \\  & ={e}^{2x}\cdot 4{e}^{2x}-2x{e}^{4x}+2{e}^{4x} \\  & =4{e}^{4x}-2x{e}^{4x}+2{e}^{4x} \\  & =6{e}^{4x}-2x{e}^{4x} \\  & =2{e}^{4x}(3-x)\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{3}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{3}=xy,{f}_{2}=0,{f}_{1}=y,$ and ${f}_{0}=2.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y={x}^{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D({x}^{3}) & =x({x}^{3})\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({x}^{3})+{x}^{3}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})+2{x}^{3} \\  & ={x}^{4}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(3{x}^{2})+{x}^{3}\cdot 3{x}^{2}+2{x}^{3} \\  & ={x}^{4}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6x)+3{x}^{5}+2{x}^{3} \\  & ={x}^{3}\cdot 6+3{x}^{5}+2{x}^{3} \\  & =6{x}^{4}+3{x}^{5}+2{x}^{3} \\  & ={x}^{3}(3{x}^{2}+6x+2)\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{3}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{3}=y,{f}_{2}=0,{f}_{1}=-xy,$ and ${f}_{0}=2.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(\operatorname{sin}⁡x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-x(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x(2-(x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=y,{f}_{1}=-2xy,$ and ${f}_{0}=3y.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y={x}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D({x}^{2}) & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({x}^{2})-2x({x}^{2})\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+3({x}^{2})^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x)-2x({x}^{2})\cdot 2x+3{x}^{4} \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot 2-4{x}^{4}+3{x}^{4} \\  & =2{x}^{2}-{x}^{4} \\  & ={x}^{2}(2-{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=y,{f}_{1}=2y,$ and ${f}_{0}=3y.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y={e}^{-2x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D({e}^{-2x}) & ={e}^{-2x}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({e}^{-2x})+2({e}^{-2x})\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-2x})+3{({e}^{-2x})}^{2} \\  & ={e}^{-2x}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{e}^{-2x})+2{e}^{-2x}\cdot (-2{e}^{-2x})+3{e}^{-4x} \\  & ={e}^{-2x}\cdot 4{e}^{-2x}-4{e}^{-4x}+3{e}^{-4x} \\  & =4{e}^{-4x}-4{e}^{-4x}+3{e}^{-4x} \\  & =3{e}^{-4x}\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=y,{f}_{1}=0,$ and ${f}_{0}=4y.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+4{(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)+4{\cos }^{2}⁡2x \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡2x(-4\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+4{\cos }^{2}⁡2x \\  & =-4{\cos }^{2}⁡2x+4{\cos }^{2}⁡2x \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{3}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{3}=x,{f}_{2}=2y,{f}_{1}=0,$ and ${f}_{0}=1.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y={x}^{3}-x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D({x}^{3}-x) & =x\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({x}^{3}-x)+2({x}^{3}-x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({x}^{3}-x)+({x}^{3}-x) \\  & =x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(3{x}^{2}-1)+2({x}^{3}-x)\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2}-1)+({x}^{3}-x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6x)+2({x}^{3}-x)\cdot (6x)+({x}^{3}-x) \\  & =x\cdot 6+12x({x}^{3}-x)+({x}^{3}-x) \\  & =12{x}^{4}+{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}+5x\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{3}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{3}=y,{f}_{2}=0,{f}_{1}=-xy,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y={e}^{x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D({e}^{x}) & ={e}^{x}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}({e}^{x})-x({e}^{x})\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}) \\  & ={e}^{x}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({e}^{x})-x{e}^{x}\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & ={e}^{x}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})-x{e}^{2x} \\  & ={e}^{x}\cdot {e}^{x}-x{e}^{2x} \\  & ={e}^{2x}(1-x)\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{3}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{3}=xy,{f}_{2}=0,{f}_{1}=0,$ and ${f}_{0}=3.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(\operatorname{sin}⁡2x) & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)+3\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+3\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)+3\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\cdot (-8\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+3\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡2x(3-8x\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)\end{aligned}
$$

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=xy,{f}_{1}=-y,$ and ${f}_{0}=4.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y={x}^{2}-3x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D({x}^{2}-3x) & =x({x}^{2}-3x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({x}^{2}-3x)-({x}^{2}-3x)\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-3x)+4({x}^{2}-3x) \\  & =x({x}^{2}-3x)\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x-3)-({x}^{2}-3x)(2x-3)+4({x}^{2}-3x) \\  & =x({x}^{2}-3x)\cdot 2-({x}^{2}-3x)(2x-3)+4({x}^{2}-3x) \\  & =2{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+6{x}^{2}-9x+4{x}^{2}-12x \\  & =7{x}^{2}-21x \\  & =7x(x-3)\end{aligned}
$$
